reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
For my lifestyle, I am profoundly disappointed in the Garmin Cirqa. 

I have an Iphone SE 3rd gen. My daily routine is three long walks with my dog. As a step counter, I do think it may be  precise, I do not think it is accurate. (My original fitbit one was probably a better pedometer.) I used to push the button to start a walking activity, however when I looked at the gps track it was garbage and was not repeatable. It would get a lower variance if I also started Open GPX Tracker. Will this get better on an Iphone 18 Pro, I have no clue. In theory that newer phone has a better gps ecology as it receives both L1 and L5 frequencies.  I have stopped using activities completely. 

At night, I wear a cpap mask. As such I lie motionless before falling asleep. The graph the next morning never shows this awake period. I am also not sure of its algorithm in parsing the measurements to determine which of the 4 modes it reports. If I just go how I feel when getting up (tired vs rested) there is not really a correlation to the sleep score. On the positive, with AI help, I used a Contec CMS50F pulse ox for a night (I do this once a month) and then had AI give me python code to pull the pulse ox data and I compared to the CMS50F and the comparison was excellent.

If I had it to do over again I would not invest in this product. That being said, Garmin could improve the app in the following areas:

1)Pulse Ox, do something like a 3 button push to get a spot reading
2) Sleep - Offer a few di

reviews.title: Buggy and dangerous
reviews.text:
I'd stopped using Garmin for cycling a few years ago because of all the bugs. But last year I crashed while alone in the woods and didn't have a computer with crash detection. So I decided to get a Garmin 1050 for the big screen and crash detection.  Fortunately I haven't needed it. But unfortunately it probably wouldn't have worked anyway. Twice now I've been going through the settings on my bike computer looking for something else and realized it said I didn't have an emergency contact so crash detection wouldn't work. It happened in March, and while I'm sure I had done it before, I redid my wife as emergency contact. And tested it to confirm the text message arrived. Just now I again found the computer said there wasn't an emergency contact and needed to set one up in the app. Checked and the app showed my wife with a verified phone number. I then verified her email and now the computer shows her verified and testing get assistance sends the phone text and email. And her phone shows the previous test from March. So I don't know when it broke, but at some point I lost that safety feature due to another Garmin bug. 

Feature bugs are one thing, but this is a safety bug. At least she would have my live track, which has never broken, but I hate that I bought a computer for a safety system that is too buggy to trust. (and I have no way of knowing whether the bug is the app or computer but the contact setup is in the app)

reviews.title: Watch out! It’s frustrating.
reviews.text:
This app leaves a lot to be desired. The UI and design language is tolerable, however the amount of bugs within this app are not. 

Currently, creating custom workouts DOES NOT work at all. Multiple times I will work my way through all of the sub menus to create one, only to click the “done” or “save” buttons that do not work. Editing the target types and rep functions glitch. I have wasted so much time trying to build workouts, edit training plans, create routes and runs. 

Everything within the application is buried in sub-menus. In search of a function within the app, sometimes a user will arrive at a menu that says “Looking for this? Actually, leave this menu and go through several other menus. This function is located on the other part of the app.”

It’s gotten so bad that I am considering selling my watch. It’s incredibly frustrating to pay a premium for a device that requires an external piece of software and equipment, only to find out that the integration between the two pieces of hardware doesn’t work. 

I am currently on the latest iteration of the application on my phone and watch:
Garmin Forerunner 265
iPhone 17 Pro

The GPS just doesn't work well where I live in London so that's not a realistic option. Very disappointed because have been using these watches for nearly 10 years and now it's broken. I won't be buying another Garmin.

Update 11 October. After an app update in the last couple of days the watch has much improved. I had nailed it down to excessive sensitivity to minor halts in arm swing, manifested in zigzags all over the pace chart, resulting in usually significant underestimates of moving time (eg losing 8 mins instead of 2 on a 20 min walk.) and hence distance. Now that’s fixed, with a slight overcompensation, walks minimally too long. But another potential update is available today and I’m reluctant to apply it and go back to how it was before, if that change was a mistake! It would be useful to know what the updates are doing before applying them

reviews.title: Fail - structured workouts
reviews.text:
I bought the Garmin Forerunner 965 specifically as a serious running and training watch, and there is a significant flaw in the way it handles structured workouts.

When you create a workout with a target pace — for example, an interval at 4:30–4:40/km — the watch bases its “Too Fast” and “Too Slow” warnings on current pace. Current GPS pace fluctuates considerably, even when you are actually running at a very consistent pace.

The result is a stream of unnecessary “Too Fast” and “Too Slow” alerts through your headphones. You can be running a perfectly well-paced interval and still have the watch repeatedly telling you that your pace is wrong.

The obvious solution is to allow the runner to select Lap Pace / Step Average Pace as the target metric. The watch already calculates and displays this data, and it provides a much more useful indication of whether you are actually on target during an interval.

The same principle should apply to heart rate: users should be able to choose whether structured-workout thresholds are evaluated against current HR or lap/step-average HR.

What makes this particularly frustrating is that Garmin’s underlying software platform already recognises lap-speed and lap-heart-rate workout target types. Yet Garmin Connect does not expose these options to ordinary users when creating workouts.

For a premium watch aimed specifically at serious runners, this is a surprisingly basic limitation.

Garmin: please add the following options to structured worko

reviews.title: Connection Error
reviews.text:
I had a very positive experience with my Garmin Forerunner 255 Music for the first year or so. It worked great and I was very happy with the watch.
Unfortunately, it then stopped connecting to my phone. I tried multiple phones/devices and went through extensive troubleshooting, which confirmed that the issue was with the watch rather than my phone.

I first reported the problem to Garmin in October 2025. After more than nine months of back-and-forth with technical support, the issue still hasn't been resolved and the watch remains unable to connect to my phone.

It's extremely disappointing to spend this much time trying to resolve an issue with a product that had previously worked so well. At this point, I'll be buying a different watch rather than continuing to pursue the problem.

The watch was great while it worked, but the lack of a solution after more than nine months of support has left me very disappointed with Garmin.

reviews.title: We need to talk..
reviews.text:
Dear Garmin,
We need to talk. Four rides out of five, you’re wonderful. My data uploads, my stats sync, my sensors connect, and I feel like the luckiest cyclist in town. You complete me. But then there’s that fifth ride. That fifth ride where I’m standing in the garage in my kit, watching the head unit search for my groupset, my lights, and my heart rate monitor like it’s never met any of them before. We’ve done this hundreds of times. The heart rate monitor is on my chest. The groupset hasn’t moved. And yet here we are, re-pairing everything like it’s the first date, while I’m already five minutes late out the door. Then I ride. And it’s glorious. Because when you work, you really work.
And then I finish. I’m tired, I’m sweaty, I want to see my numbers. And you just don’t sync! The little icon spins. I stare at it. It stares back. I’ve stood in the driveway in lycra longer than I care to admit, clicking “retry” while my neighbours quietly judge me. Here’s the thing, Garmin: I don’t believe anyone at your company actually uses this gear. Because if they did – if even one engineer had ever stood clipped in at 6am watching the head unit refuse to acknowledge that a heart rate monitor exists – this would have been fixed out of pure personal fury. Years ago.
I suspect your developers commute by bus.
So this is goodbye.
Yours, intermittently and exasperated.

reviews.title: Terrible Connect+
reviews.text:
I’ve been a subscribed member of Connect+ for the last 3 months and joined mostly for the nutrition tracking feature. 

To say that I’m disappointed would be an understatement and I can’t believe that Garmin have released this as a paid subscription feature when it is so inaccurate and should not even be out of beta. 

For example, it rarely identifies food when using the barcode scanner and when it does, the nutritional information is completely inaccurate and not reflective of what is on the food packaging. Additionally, when it does find a food but there is inaccurate nutritional information, there is no option to update or modify it. 

Also, pretty much every food item found in the database, whether it be through the barcode scanner or search function, only provides food weight at 100g, which means you have to be a mathematician whenever you want to log a food item on create a meal. Much like other nutrition tracking apps, it really needs to have options to log food as per packaging, 100g, 1g and 1 piece/item. 

To summarise, no athlete or person seriously into tracking their nutrition can or should rely on this app. It is wholly inaccurate and for a company that prides itself on supporting and improving athlete, this is diabolical at every level. 

I’ll be cancelling my Connect+ subscription until this feature is massively improved and worthy of the subscription fee … after all, Connect+ offers little else worthy of a subscription fee!

reviews.title: Deplorable update
reviews.text:
Since the latest update, this app is a black hole for data.

Activities fail to sync properly, stats are inconsistent, and in some cases data simply does not appear at all. The core purpose of the app is reliability, and right now it does not deliver.

This is coming from a long-term Garmin Fenix user. I have been using Garmin devices since the early 2010s, and this is easily the worst experience I have had.

On top of that, Garmin keeps its API locked behind restrictive developer access, which prevents users from building alternative solutions or even accessing their own data properly. If the official app is going to underperform, at least give users the flexibility to fix it themselves.

Garmin has dominated this space for years, but this update feels like a step backwards in both functionality and user trust.

Fix the fundamentals. Reliability comes first.
